Primary text: Analects 13.18, 2.7, 4.18 and 15.24, https://www.gutenberg.org/cache/epub/3330/pg3330-images.html . In 13.18 a governor praises a son for witnessing against a father who stole a sheep; Confucius values fathers and sons concealing each other. The passage does not tell us what happened to the sheep’s owner. Our return, witness, debt and repair are new case details, not an explanation that makes the original passage say something more comfortable.

Interpretation boundary: respectful correction (Analects 4.18) is discussed alongside 13.18 without claiming that this resolves their tension. Compare https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/ethics-chinese/ . Family attachment is represented as a serious claim, not merely a bias to be defeated; the owner’s loss is also not erased.

Part 2 connection: Zhuangzi’s shift of perspective and attention to circumstances, not a purported Daoist verdict on theft. https://plato.stanford.edu/entries/zhuangzi/ . The local debt, stolen sheep, missed market and informal/recorded remedies are authored, with no invented penalty presented as historical Chinese law.

Zhuangzi is conventionally associated with the fourth century BCE; the Daodejing and Analects are composite texts with debated formation histories.
